newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher led by CPI-linked bonds.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher led by CPI-linked bonds.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed broadly higher on Sunday for the fourth consecutive session, led by another sharp rise in CPI-linked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.07 pct to 103.58
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.05 pct at 102.8
Volume was moderate at 182 million shekels.

"CPI-linked bonds simply don't stop. Yields have fallen to their lowest level in years," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel (FIBI). "On inflation-linked bonds for seven years, yields fell below four percent, which is the lowest level I've ever seen."
The FIBI trader attributed the rise to the government's decision to suspend issuing inflation-linked bonds combined with the absence of sellers.
"I think yields on long bonds will continue to fall towards four percent," he said.
"I believe the main reason is that the redemptions from the provident funds have ended and now they have the inflows they need to invest," added Zvi Hoffman of Meitav Investments and Securities.

Unlinked bonds continued to rise, despite expectations for rising infaltion, with yields on unlinked bonds reaching 14.5 percent. "(This) is still attractive, if inflation remains below 10 percent," Hoffman said.
He added that if the Bank of Israel decides to leave its key lending rate unchanged at the end of this month yields will not decline any further.
Makams also rose, but traders showed only minimal interest in them, the FIBI trader said.

Dollar-linked bonds rose sharply today but traders were at a loss to explain the gain. "It might be due to speculative activity by investors who believe that the dollar will continue to rise against the shekel," the FIBI trader said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
